class: Credential guard rejects a second click made by the same authorized button
symptom: Panasonic iCIMS sign-in stayed on the password step after the accepted username and password were filled; the guard recorded credential_duplicate_click, and no site rejection was visible. The browser later also denied an asynchronous form-submit event after the first click.
site: Panasonic Automotive iCIMS/Auth0 two-step sign-in, 27 October 2026
root_cause: Auth0 dispatched another click on the same Log In button while handling the authorized Playwright click. The guard permitted only the first click and denied the site-driven second click. A separate button value=default was also treated as a visible label, blocking the authorization before the duplicate was observable. The guard also expired credential authorization at the end of the initial click task, before the site submitted the same form asynchronously. A first prevented submit event also consumed authorization before the site issued its follow-up event.
why_tests_missed: The two-step gateway fixture had no internal button value or reentrant click handler.
fix: Read only visible or accessible labels for credential buttons. Allow at most one same-button companion click in the same action during the authorized sign-in, while the form-submit event consumes authorization; map new guard denial kinds to the supported audit reason. Keep that same-form authorization for up to two seconds and wait briefly to observe the resulting form submission. A prevented first submit retains authorization for one follow-up event on the same form; a completed submit consumes it.
prevention: Test credential buttons with internal values and nested click handlers, confirming one form submission and a bounded second click.
